title: Fix bash -e swallowing health check output on exit 1
description: In health-check.yml, the 'Run health check' step uses bash -e (GHA default). When health-check.py returns exit code 1 (>50% errors), the OUTPUT= line triggers -e before echo "" runs, losing all output. Fix with || true pattern so output is always captured and displayed.
close_reason: Fixed: added || true and continue-on-error: true to 'Run health check' step so script output is always captured and displayed.

title: Fix missing Playwright system deps in health check
description: health-check.yml is missing 'install-deps chromium' step. GHA runner image update removed pre-installed libs, causing all agencies to fail. Add same install-deps step as scrape.yml.
close_reason: System deps step already exists in health-check.yml (lines 42-46) — missed on first read.

title: Strategy recommendation: demand letter vs TRO vs other
description:

## Alternatives Considered
1. Demand letters (individual agency vs batch)
2. TRO/injunction (single test case vs all 33)

acceptance_criteria: Strategy doc saved to docs/ with clear recommendation, timeline, and resource estimate.

title: Research WA legal landscape for Maass contradiction
description: Research: (1) Keep Washington Working Act enforcement history and private right of action, (2) WA Consumer Protection Act unfair/deceptive practice claims, (3) Flock Safety ToS and whether the contradiction constitutes breach of contract, (4) any existing case law on Flock data sharing or ALPR privacy in WA.
acceptance_criteria: Legal landscape memo saved to docs/ covering all four areas.
close_reason: Legal landscape memo written to docs/wa-legal-landscape.md. Key finding: SB 6002 (effective Mar 30, 2026) makes ALPR immigration enforcement violations a per se CPA violation with private right of action, treble damages, and attorneys' fees. This changes the Maass contradiction from a policy inconsistency to a potential state law violation.

acceptance_criteria: Evidence package saved to docs/ with timestamped entries for all 33 agencies.
close_reason: Evidence package compiled to docs/maass-contradiction-evidence.md — 1911 lines covering all 33 contradiction agencies with prohibited_uses, hotlists, NCIC refs, sharing partners, and external agency counts. Script at scripts/compile-evidence.py.

title: Legal strategy: Maass contradiction (33 WA agencies)

Includes evidence compilation, legal landscape research, PR requests, and strategy docs.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence package compiled for all 33 agencies. Legal landscape memo written. Strategy recommendation documented. Demand letter and/or TRO template drafted.
close_reason: All 5 child issues (c7b.1–c7b.7) closed. Evidence package, legal landscape memo, PRA requests, Snohomish/Everett deep-dive, and strategy recommendation all complete. Work product moved to private PERSONAL-legal repo for sensitive content separation.

- Export script to generate SVG/Mermaid network graphs for top multi-hop sharing chains
- Written case studies detailing major inter-state data flows (e.g., WA → ID → MN → IA)
- Integration format ready for embedding in GitHub Pages companion site and reports
notes: Focus on major regional sharing hubs (e.g., Puyallup WA PD with 45 cameras & 658k monthly reads sharing with 80+ agencies) and highlight cross-border data leakage vectors.

notes: Include state-by-state breakdowns (WA vs national), camera counts, and media-ready summaries tailored for journalists, legal researchers, and privacy advocates.

title: Deep-dive analysis: Snohomish County / Everett sharing chain
description: Detailed analysis of the Snohomish County SO policy conflict — prohibits immigration in Flock but shares directly with Everett (no Flock-level prohibition). Also trace the indirect chains through Lake Stevens and Marysville to Everett. Document the data-flow topology.
acceptance_criteria: Analysis saved to docs/ with network map and data-flow description.
close_reason: Deep-dive analysis written to docs/snohomish-everett-sharing-chain.md. Key findings: Snohomish County SO is the strongest test case (Maass contradiction + direct policy conflict with Everett). Lake Stevens and Marysville function as data routing hubs — 20 and 7 agencies respectively route through them to Everett. 33 of 41 WA agencies have data-flow paths to Everett within 3 hops.

acceptance_criteria: PRA request template drafted. Customized per agency. Ready to file.
close_reason: PRA template drafted at docs/pra-request-template.md with 7 categories of requests. 33 individualized agency-specific requests generated at docs/pra-requests/ via scripts/generate-pra-requests.py. Each includes the agency's specific prohibition text, hotlist config, sharing partners, and SB 6002 compliance inquiries.

title: Automate NCIC contradiction detection
description: Script that flags agencies in the scraper output exhibiting the Maass contradiction: those that both prohibit immigration enforcement in their policy AND subscribe to National and statewide hotlist sources (which include the NCIC Immigration Violator File). Also detect data-sharing chains to agencies like Everett/Lynnwood that don't prohibit immigration enforcement at all, since sharing data with them creates a backdoor for immigration enforcement.
notes:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Script runs against latest stats.jsonl and page.txt across all WA agencies
- Outputs report of agencies with the contradiction: prohibits immigration AND uses National/statewide hotlist sources
- Detects agencies sharing data with Everett/Lynnwood
- Results integrable into GitHub Pages or CI
close_reason: Implemented ncic-contradiction.py with 6 detection modes including indirect sharing chain graph traversal (BFS up to 5 hops). Integrated into scrape.yml workflow as 'Detect NCIC contradictions' step. Supports --commit-body for CI integration.
